title: Finite-coefficient etale exceptional normalization and its dualizing comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. Use the small pro-etale bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and its transported etale compact-support adjunction. All schemes below are finite-type $k$-schemes; their absolute separatedness is not assumed. All morphisms below are separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $\omega_h=Rh^!A$, $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\simeq Ru^!Rv^!$ for the adjunction conjugate of [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], and use the specified $\theta$ and $\beta$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] put $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,A}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$.

For every etale $e:U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], there is a canonical natural isomorphism $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$ on these categories. Its normalization is the unique right-adjoint comparison preserving the sum/evaluation counit after etale transport and the proper-support identification of compact support with the exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Put $\eta_e=\rho_{e,A}:\omega_e\simeq A_U$, inserting the coefficient-unit pullback comparison. Then:

(1) $\rho_{e,K}\theta_{e,K}$ is the unit constraint $Le^*K\otimes^L\omega_e\xrightarrow{1\otimes\eta_e}Le^*K\otimes^LA_U\simeq Le^*K$.

(2) These comparisons preserve identities and composition: for etale $e:U\to X$ and etale $v:X\to T$,
$$\rho_{ve,K}=Le^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,Rv^!K}\circ c_{v,e,K},$$
with the canonical derived-pullback composition inserted. For a Cartesian base change of $e$ along any separated finite-type $w:X'\to X$, with $e':U'\to X'$ and $w':U'\to U$, the equality $\eta_{e'}\beta_{e,w}=Lw'^*\eta_e$ holds after the coefficient-unit identifications.

(3) If $h:X\to S$ is smooth, put
$$E_{e,h}=\rho_{e,\omega_h}\circ c_{h,e,A}:\omega_{he}\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_h.$$
Then $E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}$ is the unit constraint $\omega_e\otimes^LLe^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\eta_e\otimes1}Le^*\omega_h$. For a Cartesian square $R'\xrightarrow{e'}R$, $T'\xrightarrow eT$ with vertical smooth maps $h':R'\to T'$, $h:R\to T$ and etale horizontal maps, the canonical smooth base-change map satisfies
$$\beta_{h,e}=\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}\circ E_{e',h}^{-1}:Le'^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{h'},$$
where $he'=eh'$ and the target of $\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}$ is identified with $\omega_{h'}$ using $\eta_e$.

All these identities commute with further compatible open restriction. No orientation or Tate twist is chosen.

source.place: Step 1: natural etale normalization, theta the identity and beta canonical; made precise with compact-support composition and sum/evaluation counits

proof.text: A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes every scheme in the statement Noetherian. The exceptional functors preserve the bounded constructible finite-Tor domain by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The equivalence [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies bounded etale origins, and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] makes $C_T=\nu_T^*$ fully faithful on $D^+$. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify the specified pullbacks, units and tensors through $C_T$. Compact-support composition is identified through the specified site map by [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]; exchange is transported with that normalization by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Thus an etale calculation with the transported counits gives an equality of the specified pro-etale maps; an arbitrary pro-etale input is handled by its origin isomorphism and naturality. No absolute separatedness is used. Projection maps transport as well: expand the compactification projection of [def-exchange-projection] into its proper counit-mate projection and open tensor comparison. For the proper factor the counit equality in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], tensored with the identity, identifies the defining transposes; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies their adjuncts. For the open factor the comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] is degreewise the identity on the open and zero off it, so its tensor square commutes before deriving. These equalities and the tensor comparison already cited identify the specified theta transposes.

source.place: Step 1: finite coefficients, etale-origin transport, and the named compact-support comparisons

proof.text:
On ordinary etale derived categories put $F_e=Re_!$ and $S_e=D(e_{\Sigma!})$. By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], $S_e\dashv e^*$ with the sum/evaluation counit $\operatorname{ev}_e$. Let $d_e:F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_e$ be the canonical proper-support comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] followed by its identification of proper-support sections with the sum extension; it applies because $e$ is separated etale of finite type between Noetherian schemes (Step 1), it is independent of the compactification, and it is the same comparison $c_e^c$ used in [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility] and in Step 4. Transport $S_e\dashv e^*$ along $d_e$; its counit becomes $\operatorname{ev}_e\circ d_ee^*$. For the two adjunctions $F_e\dashv e^\times$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and $S_e\dashv e^*$, the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of $d_e^{-1}:S_e\to F_e$ is the unique natural transformation $\rho_e:e^\times\to e^*$ characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\,S_e(\rho_{e,K})\,d_{e,e^\times K}=\varepsilon_{e,K},$$
so $\rho_e$ is the unique right-adjoint comparison preserving the transported counit. Conjugating an inverse gives an inverse, so this is an isomorphism without a purity theorem. Step 1 and the transported definition [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] give exactly the claimed $\rho_e$ on $D^b_{ctf}$ and its stated counit normalization. Evaluation at $A$ defines $\eta_e$, with the coefficient-unit pullback comparison inserted.

source.place: Step 1: existence and counit normalization of the etale comparison

proof.text: Write $\widehat\rho_{e,K}=\rho_{e,K}\theta_{e,K}$. Under Step 2's adjunction, the transpose of $\widehat\rho_{e,K}$ is, by [def-pur-co-smoothness](2), tensor symmetry followed by the inverse sum projection and $\operatorname{ev}_{e,A}S_e(\eta_e)\otimes1_K$. Here [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2) identifies the actual compactification projection with the sum projection, whose formula on tensor representatives is $(s,m)\otimes k\mapsto(s,m\otimes s^*k)$. The transpose of the proposed unit constraint $q=(1\otimes\eta_e)$ followed by the unitor is $\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}S_e(q)$. The two transposes agree: on a lift-indexed tensor summand both evaluate the coefficient $\eta_e(m)$ and multiply it into the restricted $k$. This is an equality of sheaf maps on representatives, and the cited projection theorem states its derived natural version, so no equality of derived maps is inferred from stalkwise equality. The adjunction bijection gives $\widehat\rho_{e,K}=q$, proving (1).

source.place: Step 1: the specified theta becomes the tensor unit map

proof.text:
Let $e,v$ both be etale. The comparison equality in [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] identifies the actual compact-support compositor, after the proper-support/sum comparisons, with the map sending nested lift-indexed summands to the composite lift. This map preserves evaluation: evaluating a nested summand and then evaluating its outer summand is evaluation of that same composite lift. Thus it is conjugate to restriction composition under the sum/evaluation adjunctions. Take conjugates using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; the conjugate of the horizontal composite of $d_v^{-1}$ and $d_e^{-1}$ for the composite adjunctions is the composite of the whiskered conjugates by the pasting clause [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2). The two successive right-adjoint comparisons are $\rho_{e,Rv^!K}$ and $e^*\rho_{v,K}$, while the compact-support compositor has conjugate $c_{v,e,K}$. Reversal of vertical composition gives
$$\rho_{ve,K}=e^*(\rho_{v,K})\rho_{e,Rv^!K}c_{v,e,K}.$$
The identity case is the identity normalization in the same proper-support theorem. Step 1 transfers this to the specified pro-etale comparisons with the canonical pullback compositor, proving the composition and unit parts of (2).

source.place: Step 1: etale comparison respects the named composition and identity maps

proof.text:
For the base change $(e,w)$, [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](1) identifies the actual compact-support exchange with the sum-extension exchange $b:w^*S_e\to S_{e'}w'^*$. This is the inverse of the map of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. Its defining conjugacy gives, at $A$ and under pullback-unit identifications,
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,A}\,b_{e^*A}^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',A}.$$
Indeed the underlying restriction/direct-image square is the fibre-product identification, and the conjugacy formula applies its unit followed by evaluation; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the resulting composite counit. By Step 2, replacing the exceptional object by $A$ with $\eta_e$ makes the transpose defining $\beta_{e,w}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness](3) exactly this equality of evaluation counits. Thus its transpose is also the transpose of $\eta_{e'}^{-1}w'^*\eta_e$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $\eta_{e'}\beta_{e,w}=w'^*\eta_e$, and Step 1 supplies its pro-etale reading.

source.place: Step 1: the eta comparison preserves arbitrary compact-support base change

proof.text:
For smooth $h$, substitute the specified definitions of $E$ and $\sigma$; the adjacent $c_{h,e,A}$ and its inverse cancel. Consequently
$$E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}=\rho_{e,\omega_h}\theta_{e,\omega_h}\operatorname{sym}.$$
Step 3 at $K=\omega_h$ identifies this with the tensor unit after $\eta_e\otimes1$, exactly the first assertion of (3). In particular $\sigma_{e,h}$ is invertible: Step 3 makes $\theta_{e,\omega_h}$ invertible, and both the symmetry and $c$ are isomorphisms. The required input $\omega_h$ is in the stated category by Step 1.

source.place: Step 1: the source-etale dualizing comparison is the unit tensor comparison

proof.text:
For any $a$ in the operation domain, $\theta_{a,A}$ is the unit constraint on $\omega_a$. Indeed the proper projection with coefficient-unit second variable is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and the open tensor comparison with the unit is the unitor; substituting in [def-exchange-projection] makes the compact-support projection a unitor. The transpose in [def-pur-co-smoothness](2) is therefore $\varepsilon_{a,A}$, whose adjunct is the identity by the triangle identity. Naturality of $\theta_{h',-}$ at $\eta_e:\omega_e\to A$ gives
$$Rh'^!(\eta_e)\theta_{h',\omega_e}=\theta_{h',A}(Lh'^*\eta_e\otimes1).$$
Substitute the definition of $\sigma_{h',e}$. Under the specified target identification by $\eta_e$, this yields
$$\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}=Rh'^!(\eta_e)c_{e,h',A}.$$
This proves its invertibility and fixes its normalization without choosing an orientation.

source.place: Step 1: tensor unit normalization needed for the target-etale factor

proof.text:
For the Cartesian square in (3), write $F=Rh_!$, $F'=Rh'_!$, $S=S_e$, $S'=S_{e'}$, $G=Rh^!$, and $G'=Rh'^!$ on the ordinary etale sites, with the exceptional functors of $e,e'$ replaced by $e^*,e'^*$ through Step 2. Let $C:e^*F\to F'e'^*$ be the specified exchange, and $\delta:FS'\to SF'$ the composition comparison of [lem-pur-etale-horizontal-support-mate]. Define
$$b=G'(\eta_e)c_{e,h',A}c_{h,e',A}^{-1}\rho_{e',GA}^{-1}:e'^*GA\to G'A.$$
Let $t: FGA\to A$ and $t':F'G'A\to A$ be the exceptional counits. Expanding the two composite counits using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the normalized conjugate comparisons, the mate-pasting equation [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3) is
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,A}\,S(t'F'b)=t\,F(\operatorname{ev}_{e',GA})\,\delta_{e'^*GA}^{-1}.$$
Here $F'b$ means application of the functor $F'$ to $b$. All terms have source $SF'e'^*GA$ and target $A$. This identifies the actual map $b$ through its composite counit, not through an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism.

source.place: Step 1: explicit composite-counit equation for the Cartesian etale square

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-etale-horizontal-support-mate] at $M=GA$ to the right side of Step 8. It becomes
$$t\,\operatorname{ev}_{e,FGA}\,S(C_{GA}^{-1})=\operatorname{ev}_{e,A}\,S(e^*t\,C_{GA}^{-1}),$$
where the equality is naturality of the evaluation counit at $t:FGA\to A$. Injectivity of the $S\dashv e^*$ Hom bijection in [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] cancels this common evaluation operation from Step 8, yielding
$$t'F'b=e^*t\,C_{GA}^{-1}.$$
By [def-pur-co-smoothness](3), the right side is the defining transpose of $\beta_{h,e}$. The $F'\dashv G'$ bijection gives $b=\beta_{h,e}$. Steps 6--7 rewrite $b$ as $\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}E_{e',h}^{-1}$ with exactly the unit identification in the statement. Step 1 transfers the equality to the specified pro-etale maps. Finally compatible open restriction preserves these constructions: exchange respects pasted squares and composition by [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), the support/projection comparisons have their stated base-change normalization, and taking mates respects pasting by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Substitution into the same counit equations proves every displayed identity after any further compatible open restriction. No twist or orientation entered any equation.

split_report.summary: Made explicit that both morphisms in the rho composition law are etale (rho_v is otherwise undefined). Normalized rho and theta via ordinary etale sum/evaluation adjunctions and transported the specified maps. Reused the existing quasi-finite proper-support compositor theorem. Extracted one genuinely new left-adjoint comparison: the mate of the specified compact-support exchange in an etale-horizontal square. The smooth square is an explicit double-counit calculation, and source-etale tensor compatibility is cancellation. No purity orientation or SGA source is used.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the ancestor thm-pur-composition-coherence proof Step 1 sentence on compatibility of smooth-base-change/co-projection factors with composition, through main-20261015 co-smooth-etale-locality proof Step 1.

tool_uses.why: Expands the specified proper/open compact-support projection, rather than substituting an arbitrary projection isomorphism.
